draft.title: Change and continuity in America
card: Change means something was different at the end of a period from the start. Continuity means something stayed much the same. Historians judge both by comparing two dates, here 1754 and 1789.
In 1754 the colonies were ruled by Britain and its king. By 1789 the United States was a republic with its own constitution, elected leaders and separated powers.
Slavery continued in much of the new nation. Women still had few political rights, and wealthy white men still held most power in society.
A revolution can change government greatly and leave much of society as it was. Judging it means weighing both, not choosing one.
draft.remember: Between 1754 and 1789 government changed greatly, but much of society stayed the same.

a.q: Which of these is an example of continuity between 1754 and 1789?
opts: Slavery continued in much of the colonies and the new nation
Britain no longer ruled the thirteen colonies
The new nation wrote a constitution of its own
Americans elected leaders instead of obeying a king
a.why: Slavery was present in 1754 and still present in 1789, so it stayed the same. The other options describe government, which was different by 1789, so they show change.
a.clue: Look for something that was the same at both dates.

b.q: A student claims the American Revolution changed everything in colonial life. Which reply best uses the idea of change and continuity?
opts: Government changed greatly, but slavery still continued
Society changed greatly, but Britain still ruled government
Government and society both stayed the same over the period
Government changed little, but slavery ended across the nation
b.why: By 1789 government had changed from British rule to a republic, yet slavery remained. The second option reverses this, placing the change in society and the continuity in government.
b.clue: Check which parts of America were different in 1789 and which were not.

a.q: Which of these is an example of continuity between 1754 and 1789?
opts: Wealthy white men held most power in society
The nation was a republic with no king at its head
The nation was governed under its own constitution
Power was split between separate branches
a.why: Wealthy white men held most power in 1754 and still did in 1789, so this stayed the same. A republic, a national constitution and separated powers were all new by 1789, so they show change, not continuity.
a.clue: Which one was true in 1754 as well as in 1789?

b.q: A student claims the American Revolution changed everything in colonial life. Which reply best uses the idea of change and continuity?
opts: Government changed greatly, but slavery largely remained
Society changed greatly, but Britain still ruled
Government and society both stayed much the same
Government changed little, but slavery ended everywhere
b.why: By 1789 government had changed from British rule to a republic, yet slavery remained in much of the nation. The reply that society changed while Britain still ruled reverses this: Britain no longer ruled by 1789, and much of society stayed the same.
b.clue: Check which parts of America were different in 1789 and which were not.
